title: So you think you look good? (Physique Critique Chad Edition)
summary: A three-hour livestream where NH reviews 20 subscriber physiques, mixed with chat Q&A. For each physique he points out lagging muscles and gives cut/bulk/recomp advice, and he keeps coming back to a few ideas: abs are almost always underdeveloped, back dominance is common, genetic potential stays hidden until you train, and dirty bulks are a mistake. In the Q&A he also covers his own cardio, calf training, arm measurements and the lifts he has dropped.
claims: Michael Gundill, who works with enhanced pro bodybuilders, rated a top French natural a 6; NH says by those standards he himself would be a 3, and people who see enhanced muscle daily can recognize natural muscle
Benching two days in a row is a bad idea even with different variations because it trains the same muscle group; 48 hours between sessions for a muscle is a bare minimum

He does not plan on TRT later in life: his body produces plenty of testosterone now, he has seen men in their 50s-60s doing fine without exogenous hormones, and he believes testosterone declines with age for a reason
After a year away from the gym, pick up where you left off but slowly, with less volume; that is the price to pay
He runs on a self-powered (non-motorized) treadmill where your stride sets the pace; he holds a 10-minute mile for one mile and aims for a 7-minute mile

His hardest cardio is the stair machine on tiptoes, stepping only on the edge of the step, with an 80 lb backpack for 10 minutes at moderate pace; it works as high-intensity cardio and also hammers the calves
His moderate-intensity cardio is weighted carries for distance in his backyard
If he ever cuts, it would be to see his body without the fluff, not to look good on social media
His calf training: progressive overload on two calf raise variations (SSB and belt squat), tibialis raises at least 3x/week, plus cardio and tiptoe carries with a 100 lb metal stone
His calves grew from 16 in (2020) to 17 in (around 2022) to about 17.8 in on the right side
Calves and arms can't be compared: even 18-19 in calves still look small, and he thinks his will only look big at about 20 in
Most people have good calf insertions; anyone who has never trained calves can't judge their insertion because the muscle isn't big enough to show it, and the same goes for lats
Big calves usually come from being heavy when young or from genetics; he had neither and had to train them

He dropped the bench press after repeated shoulder injuries; his chest originally grew from push-ups at home and he only went back to benching because of powerlifting dogma; ring push-ups and dips are S-tier
The bench press is not bad for bodybuilding; try it, and if it agrees with your body keep it, otherwise use something else
Somatotypes are nonsense; morphology (long or short arms, torso and so on) is real and shapes both how you look and how you move; he went from 'ectomorph' when skinny to 'mesomorph' when fat
At 5'10 instead of his height, carrying the same muscle he would weigh around 190-195 lb
A burnt-out ex-athlete should restart bit by bit with the activity he used to love; hypertrophy training will then improve that sport and get the ball rolling
Ethiopians tend to have long physiques with long legs, but that doesn't stop them building muscle; the viewer who doubted it had already built a good physique
Lack of core development is the most common weakness he sees: at lean body fat the abs should be clearly visible, and abs that show only when skinny are not hypertrophied, so isolate them
A physique with no major fat to lose needs neither a cut nor a hard bulk: recomp or slow bulk and target the lagging muscles
The waist dictates upper-body proportions: on a slim waist, every bit of size added to the shoulders looks doubled
If the chest dominates and the shoulders lag, skew the program toward vertical pressing, cut back on horizontal pressing, and isolate the side and rear delts
Tall, long-legged lifters must hammer their legs because long legs look slim even when developed
Former athletes who start lifting tend to progress very fast
Back dominance is surprisingly common across his 30-40 reviews, possibly caused by the nonsense idea that you should do twice as much pulling as pushing
A wide waist can work if the upper body is thick enough that nobody looks at the waist
Triceps long-head development seen from the back is underrated
Arm measurements mislead: short arms with a long triceps sweep make a 17 in arm look like 19 in
Many lifters, including himself, started bodybuilding to impress a girl they never got, then fell in love with training
He only features physiques that look achievable naturally; if someone reached them with drugs, they took a risk for something they could have got anyway
Gaining about 15 kg in two years (58 to 74 kg at 176 cm) is realistic for most people who start skinny
If hip hinges all go to your glutes, bias the hamstrings with hyperextensions, leg curls, and RDLs with the bar pushed against the quads so the knees can't bend
Push/pull/legs has a bad reputation online but is a very good split to grow on
Beginners training abs should start at twice a week and work up to three times
Going from 144 to 187 lb in a few months means you got fat; cut
For an underdeveloped posterior chain, start leg days with a posterior chain movement you enjoy: good mornings, any RDL variation, hyperextensions
The ideal bodybuilding height is about 5'7 to 5'9: not stocky, yet short enough to fill out quickly; most taller guys at his gym are skinny because they're lankier
A recomp is a test of patience because progress is judged on gym performance
If you start fat, cut until you are skinny-fat or skinny and then build; if you are already skinny-fat, cutting is a mistake
With very wide hip bones, build the obliques, lats, core, chest and shoulders so people don't look at the hips
Reverse lunges can replace RDLs; they're underrated and are a different movement, not a weaker lunge
The neck standard is in line with the jaw; much more than that makes you look like a ball
A former elite-level powerlifter who got hurt and switched to bodybuilding built an excellent physique while running a company, proof that you don't need to live in the gym
Skiing builds the legs to a large extent
Skinny beginners with tube-shaped arms often turn out to have great genetics that nobody could see before training: ignore your genetics and train, and you may be surprised
A naturally tiny waist is an asset to preserve: no dirty bulks, only lean bulking
Vascularity, and whether veins sit on the surface of the arm, is genetic
People who don't send leg pictures usually have small legs; don't become an upper-body bro with bird legs, so do split squats and posterior chain work
Bodybuilding is about illusions: a lean 5'8 lifter at 165 lb can look huge
A young natural doing everything right can reach 180-190 lb lean and will then get steroid accusations that look justified
Lifts he has dropped: standing curls, most free-weight triceps work (now mostly cables and Smith), the bench press, and the overhead press
He replaced the overhead press with an 80-degree incline press on the Smith machine because he can progress on it; a lift you can't progress on is a bad lift
There is no upside to sitting around 22% body fat unless you are a strongman chasing every pound; if you already carry the weight, bulking is redundant
Always track PRs, especially if your goal is strength
When the shoulders dominate the arms, cut back on vertical pressing and favor horizontal pressing and vertical pulling
A big neck is usually a good sign of muscle-building potential, but with a square jawline don't overtrain the neck so it doesn't hide the jaw
Upper back rounding on heavy squats or RDLs can come from core weakness, poor technique cues, or simply not being built for those lifts; try other squat and hinge variations
Neck training with poor posture can make the posture worse; before neck flexions, tuck the chin back to reinforce good posture
Good posture starts as an intention: shoulders back, chin tucked, eyes forward, screens at eye level, imagine a string pulling the head up; training the traps also helps pull the shoulders back
Bad posture makes you look lazy and unkempt; his upright posture impressed a headmaster and got him into a top Paris high school
When two muscles compete on presses, the dominant one stays dominant; to grow the chest past dominant shoulders, use flyes and ring push-ups
A torso-dominant physique left alone becomes a spider physique; add arm isolation now and hit the legs hard
Once you can do 20+ bodyweight pull-ups, move to weighted pull-ups; weighted calisthenics is the way
He dislikes strength standards as a way to judge progress
The lean athletic physique is easy to settle for, but reaching a bodybuilder physique means going through an awkward bulking phase where you look worse
A skinny pack is not a six-pack: abs that show only because you're lean have no muscle, so isolate them for years even when they don't show
Aggressive dirty bulking adds unneeded fat and can hurt skin quality; you then have more to cut, and some people never lose the love handles
Lighting, pump, posing and camera make a huge difference: the same lifter can look like a gremlin or a bodybuilder
If your structure is poor for bodybuilding (wide waist), don't chase the shredded look; pack on as much mass as possible and hide the structure
The yoke (traps and neck) is what makes a bulky physique look powerful instead of fat
With a wide waist, isolate the obliques as much as possible so the waist at least looks freaky
Most women he knows prefer a bulkier physique to a shredded one; it's also easier to maintain and looks better in clothes
Very fat people often keep cutting past the point of need; once fat is under control, start a lean bulk
Alternating bulking and maintenance phases is smart, and it's what he is doing now
At a heavy bodyweight where more gaining just adds fat, a long recomp of one to two years is the right move
Strength doesn't equal size: a 216 lb lifter with big delts benches only 205, squats 250, RDLs 275 and overhead presses 145 lb; what matters is that performance trends up
The absolute number he lifts now matters less than the number he will lift in six months; his squats and RDLs aren't crazy but they trend up
Skinny-fat lifters usually become normal or skinny through a recomp rather than a cut
If your proportions don't suit the deadlift, drop it entirely and train the posterior chain with other movements
Long biceps and triceps insertions are a blessing in disguise: big size potential, even though they look small while undeveloped
The taller you are, the harder it is to look big; a 6'2-6'3 man will likely end up around 220-250 lb at his peak
Tall lifters can justify more aggressive bulking, e.g. 75 to 95 kg in three years
For bicep-dominant lifters with lagging shoulders: progress on vertical presses and do cable lateral raises with a cuff, watching that trap-dominant people don't shrug the weight up
People who store fat on their back usually have big back potential and should build it rather than cut
Lifting while losing fat keeps the skin firmer and reduces stretch marks; fat loss is only half the fight and muscle building is the rest
A formerly obese reviewee lost about 40 kg by walking and intermittent fasting, then started lifting
For complete legs on lifters with dominant outer quads, put more emphasis on the VMO and adductors
To get past the lean 'auto mode' physique, most people must go through a bulk; you can't magically go straight to jacked without steroids
Gaining 45 lb in four years (140 to 185 lb) is doable only with very good genetics; a first-ever deadlift of 355 lb at 150 lb bodyweight shows a gifted lifter
Once you build your body with average genetics, you realize there are people with far better genetics; a 185 lb natural might rate a 7
Genetics decides how long you stay looking skinny, not whether you get out of it; for him it took years
Men enter their prime in their 30s, so don't panic at 23; just train through your 20s
If the forearms are very dominant, reduce pronated curls; the rows already train elbow flexion, so focus on the biceps
Pronounced peaks and valleys between muscles show genetic potential, even when overall size is small
If you want to cut because of body dysmorphia, cut once and then focus on lean bulking, because what you need is mass
Not having a program, or doing abs 'when I can', means skipping them; put abs in the program and superset them with your favorite press
A flat 'fridge back' comes from neglecting vertical pulling
He recommends a 6 ft, 220 lb high-fat lifter cut 15-20 lb while improving pull-ups and arm isolation; to be lean himself, NH would need to lose at least 15 lb
If the triceps or brachioradialis overpower the biceps, favor pure supination work over pronated movements
